findings.rationale: The comparison is backwards. It returns True only after the window has closed (age over 30 days) and False for every order inside it. The docstring and linked issue #48 both say a refund is allowed up to and including day 30, so the check should be `age_days <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS`. You may also want to reject a negative age (placed_on after today) with `0 <= age_days <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS`.
This new refund-eligibility logic has no tests, which is how the inverted comparison got through. Add tests for day 0, day 30 (allowed), day 31 (refused) and a future placed_on date.

The comparison is backwards. This returns True only after the window has closed (day 31 or later) and False for days 0 through 30. Issue #48 asks for refunds to be allowed up to and including day 30, and refused after that. The docstring says the same as the issue. Use `age_days <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS` instead. To also reject a `placed_on` date in the future, use `0 <= age_days <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS`.
There are no tests for `can_refund`. A boundary test would have caught the inverted comparison. Add tests for day 0, day 30 (allowed) and day 31 (refused).

The comparison is backwards. `age_days > REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS` returns True only once the order is older than 30 days. So every order inside the window, day 30 included, is refused, and every expired order is allowed. Issue #48 asks for refunds up to and including day 30, and the function's own docstring says the same. Change the check to `age_days <= REFUND_WINDOW_DAYS`. Consider also returning False when `age_days` is negative, which happens if `placed_on` is after `today`.

The new refund-window logic ships without any tests. A test at the boundaries (day 0, day 30, day 31, and a future-dated order) would have caught the reversed comparison on line 13. Add unit tests for `can_refund` covering these cases.
